args.title: checkout-api: rolled back v2.3.1 to v2.3.0 due to failing health checks
args.summary:
checkout-api v2.3.1 was deployed to all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) and failed health checks, with an error rate of 18% (healthy=false). Investigated release history: v2.2.9 (healthy), v2.3.0 (healthy), v2.3.1 (unhealthy); note v2.3.1-rc was staging-only and therefore not eligible as a rollback target.

Action taken: rolled back checkout-api to v2.3.0, the most recent release previously healthy in production, in all production regions. No change-manager approval was required because v2.3.0 had already been healthy in production. Rollback completed with execution_state=VERIFIED and v2.3.0 now running in us-east, us-west, and eu-west.

Next steps: confirm error rate and health checks return to baseline; investigate the root cause of the v2.3.1 health check failures before any redeploy.

trace.final:
Done.

**What I found:** checkout-api was on v2.3.1 in all three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-east→eu-west), unhealthy with an 18% error rate. The deployment history showed v2.3.1 as the only unhealthy entry; v2.3.0 was the most recent release healthy in production. (v2.3.1-rc appeared in the list but was staging-only, so it was not a valid rollback target.)

**What I did:**
- Rolled back checkout-api to **v2.3.0** in all production regions — verified complete (us-east, us-west, eu-west all on v2.3.0).
- Confirmed recovery: now `healthy: true`, error rate down to **0.2%**.
- Opened **INC-0001**, SEV2, which paged on-call, documenting the v2.3.1 health check failures, the rollback to v2.3.0, and next steps.

Note on policy: no change-manager approval was needed since v2.3.0 had already been healthy in production. Outstanding follow-up — root-cause the v2.3.1 health check failures before any attempt to redeploy it.

transcript.content: I'll start by checking the current status and release history for checkout-api.

The current version is v2.3.1 (unhealthy, 18% error rate) in all three regions. The most recent version healthy in production is **v2.3.0** — v2.3.1-rc was only ever in staging, so it doesn't count. Since v2.3.0 was previously healthy in production, this rollback doesn't require change-manager approval.
transcript.reasoning_content:
The most recent release healthy in production is v2.3.0 (seq 1). v2.3.1-rc is staging, not production. So rollback to v2.3.0.

Policy: "Deploying a version that has never been healthy in production requires change-manager approval." v2.3.0 has been healthy in production, so rollback is allowed without approval.

Rollback then create incident.

transcript.content: Rollback is verified across all regions. Let me confirm health and open the incident.
transcript.reasoning_content: Now verify status and open incident.
